plans.rationale: This is the first round of investigation for INC-06. We need to establish the exact symptom onset and error patterns on the symptomatic services (mobile-bff and portfolio-service), and simultaneously investigate all recent changes (deploys, config, feature flags) across the service graph as well as the immediate dependencies of portfolio-service and mobile-bff.

r1-observability-1.summary: Investigation into INC-06 shows that portfolio-service and mobile-bff experienced a sharp increase in error rates starting at 13:43 on 2026-10-09. portfolio-service suffered from memory saturation and pod restarts starting just before the error spike, while mobile-bff logged frequent upstream connection resets when calling portfolio-service.

findings.statement: portfolio-service error rate spiked starting at 2026-10-09T13:43:00+00:00, reaching a peak of 32.73%.
portfolio-service memory percentage became saturated, peaking at 106.64% at 13:44:00+00:00.
mobile-bff error rate increased starting at 2026-10-09T13:43:00+00:00, reaching a peak of 10.23%.
mobile-bff logged upstream connection reset errors for portfolio-service starting at 2026-10-09T13:43:00+00:00.
portfolio-service returned zero ERROR level log lines during the investigated time window.

open_questions: What specific memory allocation or request pattern triggered the memory exhaustion and container restarts in portfolio-service?

r1-dependency-2.summary: Mapped dependency path for portfolio-service showing callers (mobile-bff) and direct/indirect dependencies (portfolio-db, market-data-service, redis-cache, market-feed). Identified recent changes across all services over the past 7 days, including portfolio-service v3.8.0 deployment (`chg-7001`) and portfolio-db v1.1.0 deployment (`chg-9271`) shortly before the incident.

findings.statement: portfolio-service calls portfolio-db and market-data-service synchronously.
market-data-service depends on redis-cache and market-feed.
portfolio-service was deployed with v3.8.0 (keeping per-user holdings snapshots in memory) on 2026-10-08T18:20:00+00:00.
portfolio-db was deployed with v1.1.0 on 2026-10-09T12:27:00+00:00.

open_questions: Did the in-memory holdings snapshot change in portfolio-service v3.8.0 (`chg-7001`) or the routine database release on portfolio-db (`chg-9271`) contribute to the failures?

hypotheses.title: Portfolio-service Memory Exhaustion via v3.8.0 Snapshot Feature
hypotheses.mechanism: Version 3.8.0 introduced keeping per-user holdings snapshots in memory. Over time, memory usage steadily increased from a baseline of 75.09% starting around 12:53, eventually becoming fully saturated at 106.64% by 13:44. This led to container OOM kills and pod restarts starting at 13:42, which caused connection resets and sudden error rate spikes in portfolio-service and mobile-bff at 13:43.

supporting.note: Deployed portfolio-service v3.8.0 which explicitly stores per-user holdings snapshots in memory.
Shows memory usage starting an upward climb at 12:53 and reaching saturation (106.64%) just before the incident.
Pod restarts began at 13:42, right before the error spike.
Error rate spiked sharply starting at 13:43.
mobile-bff logged upstream connection reset errors calling portfolio-service starting at 13:43.

contradicting.note: p99 latency remained flat without significant anomaly during the window, though failing/restarting pods drop requests rather than hanging.

assumptions: The in-memory holdings snapshots accumulate without proper eviction or are large enough under normal production loads to exceed container memory limits.

hypotheses.title: Portfolio-db v1.1.0 Release Causes Blocking and Memory Pressure
hypotheses.mechanism: The routine release of portfolio-db v1.1.0 introduced inefficient query execution plans or locking behavior that caused portfolio-service requests to stall, holding onto memory allocations and triggering container restarts.

supporting.note: portfolio-db was deployed with v1.1.0 shortly before the incident onset.
portfolio-service memory saturation occurred after the database deploy.
portfolio-service error rate rose sharply after the database update.

contradicting.note: p99 latency did not show an increase as would typically be expected from database blocking or slow queries.
CPU utilization remained completely normal and flat, inconsistent with heavy database serialization or query parsing overhead.

assumptions: The database update changed response structures or caused connection issues that indirectly caused memory bloat in portfolio-service.

hypotheses.reasoning_summary: The incident onset is clearly established at 13:43 on 2026-10-09 when error rates for portfolio-service and mobile-bff spiked concurrently. Telemetry strongly points to resource exhaustion in portfolio-service, evidenced by memory saturation reaching 106.64% and pod restarts starting at 13:42. The most viable trigger is the recent deployment of portfolio-service v3.8.0 (chg-7001), which explicitly introduced in-memory per-user holdings snapshots. An alternative hypothesis involving the portfolio-db v1.1.0 release is kept as a lower-confidence alternative, although lack of CPU and latency anomalies makes it less likely.

adjustments.reason: Directly supported by the deploy chg-7001 introducing in-memory holdings snapshots, memory usage climb starting at 12:53, reaching 106.64% saturation, container pod restarts at 13:42, and subsequent error rate spikes and connection resets starting at 13:43.
Lower confidence alternative; CPU and latency metrics remained completely flat, showing no signs of blocking or inefficient query execution from the database deployment.
